questions.def: Scarcely/Hardly/Barely...than' indicates an immediate subsequent event.
questions.question: ___ had I sat down than the phone rang.

questions.def: "Little" begins a sentence emphasizing lack of awareness, triggering inversion.
questions.question: ___ did she suspect that she was being followed.

questions.def: Inversion requires auxiliary verb before the subject: "Never have I seen..."
questions.question: Never I have seen such beauty in nature.

questions.def: "Only later" requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: Only later ___ the full implications of his decision.

questions.def: "On no account" is a negative adverbial requiring inversion.
questions.question: ___ under any circumstances should you open the door.

questions.def: "Had" introduces a conditional clause with inversion.
questions.question: ___ had the chemical been contained, the consequences would have been dire.

questions.def: "Not until then" requires inversion after the phrase.
questions.question: Not ___ did she appreciate his sacrifice.

questions.def: "Under no circumstances" needs inversion to express strong negation.
questions.question: ___ do I want to see that film again!

questions.def: "Had" introduces a conditional clause, inverted form.
questions.question: ___ I known, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: "Little" requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: Little ___ the trouble that awaited us.

questions.def: "No sooner...than" indicates an immediate sequence and requires inversion.
questions.question: ___ had they arrived than the meeting began.

questions.def: "Should" introduces a conditional clause with inversion in formal style.
questions.question: ___ should you require further assistance, please contact us.

questions.def: "At no time" requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: At no time ___ that he was involved.

questions.def: "Only now" requires inversion when it starts the sentence.
questions.question: ___ is the extent of the damage caused by the storm.

questions.def: "Were" creates an inverted conditional, more formal than "If".
questions.question: ___ the resources available, we will succeed.

questions.def: "Seldom" requires inversion to express infrequency of action.
questions.question: Seldom ___ such a magnificent sight.

questions.def: "Only then" at start means inversion is needed.
questions.question: ___ did the audience realise the play's significance.

questions.def: "Were" starts an inverted conditional clause.
questions.question: ___ I able to help, I certainly would.

questions.def: "Rarely" necessitates an inverted sentence structure.
questions.question: Rarely ___ to see him again.

questions.def: "Hardly…than" indicates near simultaneous events with inversion.
questions.question: ___ had the rain stopped than the sun appeared.

questions.def: "Should" introduces a formal conditional with subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: ___ the situation to escalate, we must act now.

questions.def: "At no point" requires inversion in the main clause.
questions.question: At no point ___ such resistance.

questions.def: "Little" at sentence start means auxiliary-subject inversion.
questions.question: ___ aware of the risks, they continued their expedition.

questions.def: "Should" enables a formal conditional with subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: ___ the opportunity arise, I will seize it.

questions.def: Inversion with 'scarcely' requires 'had' before the subject.
questions.question: ___ had I sat down than the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ leave the building.

questions.def: 'Rarely' necessitates inversion with the auxiliary verb 'is'.
questions.question: ___ such dedication be seen.

questions.def: 'Never' at the beginning requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: ___ do I want to see that film again!

questions.def: 'Only after' requires inversion of the main clause.
questions.question: Only ___ the research, can we proceed.

questions.def: 'Little' requires subject-auxiliary inversion, hence 'Little did'.
questions.question: ___ she know what was coming.
